text: This paper examines the issue of power flow in electrical circuits,  -  focusing on situations where power surges occur in the opposite direction to traditional flow – a phenomenon known as inverse power flow. This unconventional problem has gained significance due to the increasing integration of distributed generation units,  -  solar panels, into power systems. The study introduces a comprehensive mathematical model,  -  constraints on voltage and power limits, and proposes an efficient solution method based on optimization algorithms, to determine the pattern of inverse power flow. Case studies conducted in this research highlight the real-world implications and potential for the management of power systems. And pave the way for more precise and efficient manipulation of power flow in complex electrical grids. Future implications of managing inverse power flow and its importance in the development of smart grid technologies are also explored.

Georgia's government has announced plans to introduce a hidden asset pardon, allowing individuals to declare any undisclosed assets without facing criminal charges. This move is part of the country's ongoing efforts to combat corruption and promote transparency.  Under the proposed scheme, individuals who voluntarily disclose their hidden assets will be exempt from prosecution, and will only be required to pay a fine. The fine will be based on the value of the assets declared, with higher penalties for larger amounts.  The government hopes the hidden asset pardon will encourage individuals to come forward and declare any undisclosed wealth, thereby increasing tax revenues and reducing corruption. It is estimated that billions of dollars are hidden in offshore accounts and other undisclosed assets in Georgia.  The initiative is part of a broader anti-corruption campaign launched by the government. Which has been praised by international organizations  -  Transparency International. Georgia has made significant progress , in recent years, in tackling corruption and improving its business environment. But hidden assets remain a major challenge.  Critics argue that the hidden asset pardon could be seen as a lenient approach, , towards individuals who have evaded taxes and engaged in corrupt practices. They argue that a more stringent approach. Including criminal charges and asset seizures, would be more effective in deterring such behavior.  However, supporters of the scheme believe that it strikes a balance between encouraging individuals to come forward and punishing those who continue to hide their assets. They argue that the prospect of avoiding criminal charges and paying a fine will incentivize individuals to disclose their hidden wealth, leading to increased tax revenues and a more transparent economy.  The government plans to launch an awareness campaign to inform the public about the hidden asset pardon and the benefits of coming forward. It will also establish a dedicated unit within the tax authorities to handle the disclosure process and ensure that individuals are treated fairly.  The introduction of the hidden asset pardon is seen as a significant step towards strengthening Georgia's anti-corruption efforts and promoting a more transparent business environment. It remains to be seen how effective the scheme will be in encouraging individuals to disclose their hidden assets and whether it will have a lasting impact on reducing corruption in the country.

Prime Minister Boris Johnson announced his resignation from his position in June, marking the end of his three-year leadership of the United Kingdom.  In a statement delivered outside 10 Downing Street, Johnson informed the Queen of his decision earlier in the day. He expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve and acknowledged the weight of responsibility that comes with being prime minister.  "It has been an immense privilege to serve as your prime minister," Johnson said. "I have always tried my best to live up to the trust placed in me by the British people and to do what I think is right for our country."  Johnson's departure comes amid mounting pressure following a series of scandals and controversies that have marred his time in office. A growing number of Conservative MPs had called for his resignation, citing concerns over his leadership style and handling of key issues, including Brexit and the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.  The PM's announcement was met with mixed reactions from politicians and the public. Some colleagues praised Johnson's commitment to public service, while critics welcomed his exit. Opposition leaders called for a general election, arguing that the country needs fresh leadership and a new direction.  The timeline for Johnson's departure is unclear, but it is expected that he will officially step down at the end of June. The process for selecting a new Conservative Party leader – and by extension, the next prime minister – will likely begin shortly thereafter. Several names are already circulating as potential successors, including prominent cabinet members such as Chancellor Rishi Sunak and Home Secretary Priti Patel.  As the UK prepares for this transition, many are reflecting on Johnson's legacy. Supporters point to some notable achievements during his tenure, such as securing a withdrawal agreement with the European Union.

Arie Lev Gruzman (Hebrew, ארי לעבד גרוזמן, born July 1, 1948) is an American academic and scholar of Jewish studies. He is currently the director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University.  Gruzman was born in Tel Aviv, Israel, to a family of Holocaust survivors. He received his undergraduate degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1969, and his Ph.D. in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations from Harvard University in 1977.  After completing his doctorate, Gruzman held academic positions at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of California, Berkeley, before joining the faculty at Georgetown in 1985. At Georgetown, he has served as the director of the Center for Jewish Studies since 1995.  Gruzman's research interests include Jewish history, Jewish thought, and the relationship between Judaism and Christianity. He has published numerous articles and books on these topics, including "The Jews and the Dead Sea Scrolls" (1992) and "The Jewish Jesus, How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament" (2000).  In addition to his academic work, Gruzman has been involved in several interfaith initiatives; He has served as a consultant to the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue, and has been a member of the National Council of Churches' Committee on Faith and Order.  Gruzman has also been active in promoting Jewish-Muslim dialogue. In 2008, he co-founded the Georgetown-Sultan Qabas University Dialogue Initiative, which brings together students and scholars from both institutions to engage in dialogue and learning about each other's faiths.  Throughout his career, Gruzman has been recognized for his contributions to Jewish studies and interfaith dialogue. In 2012, he was awarded the National Jewish Book Award for his book "The Jewish Jesus, How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament." He has also received numerous honors and awards from various organizations.

This paper introduces a topological image segmentation technique for automatic sign language recognition. It employs the watershed transformation to derive the topological derivative from the gradient magnitude of video frames; However, the gradient magnitude does not meet the topological derivative's requirements, so an isotropic filter is applied to normalize its values. This approach enhances the watershed-based segmentation technique's effectiveness and robustness. Subsequently, regions are classified using statistical features from the normalized RGB histogram; Feature selection is then performed using the Fisher score to reduce dimensionality and identify the most relevant features for classification. Finally, the k-NN classifier is used for the classification of gesture sequences. The proposed method has been validated using the Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database, achieving a recognition rate of 95.6%.

Ingredients, For the dumplings One 16-ounce package of square dumpling wrappers or round wrappers 1 pound crabmeat 1/2 cup all-purpose flour 2 tablespoons minced green onion 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 tablespoon sake or dry sherry 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper 1/2 cup thinly sliced green onion tops  For the dipping sauce 1/4 cup soy sauce 1 tablespoon rice vinegar 1 tablespoon honey 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger  Instructions 1. In a large bowl, mix together the crabmeat. Flour, minced green onion, minced ginger, soy sauce, sake or sherry, sesame oil, salt and pepper. 2. Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper. (Save any leftover filling for another use.) 3. Dip your finger into water and moisten the edges of the wrapper. Fold opposite corners together, pressing to seal. Arrange filled dumplings on a baking sheet dusted with flour. 4. Prepare a basket steamer. Stack the dumplings touching but not overlapping. Cover and steam for about 10 minutes until the wrappers are cooked through and the filling is hot. 5. In a small bowl, mix all dipping sauce ingredients and whisk to blend. 6. Arrange hot dumplings on a plate and sprinkle with green onion tops. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

The Fife Coalfield was a significant coal mining region in Scotland, primarily located in Fife and extending into neighboring counties of Angus and Kinross. Historically, it played a crucial role in the economic development of Fife, providing employment for many years.  The first coal mine in the area was established in 1575, and the industry experienced rapid growth during the 18th and 19th centuries. At its peak, the Fife Coalfield boasted over 300 mines, making it one of the most productive coal mining regions in the United Kingdom.  The Fife Coalfield began to decline in the early 20th century due to increasing competition from other energy sources. The last coal mine in the area closed in 1966, marking the end of the industry. Today, the Fife Coalfield is remembered as an important part of Fife's history, with numerous artifacts and monuments commemorating the industry. The Scottish Mining Museum in Newtongrange attracts many visitors, and the area is also home to several heritage sites dedicated to the coal miners of the Fife Coalfield.

"The Last Children of Schewenborn" is a chilling post-apocalyptic novel that delves into the aftermath of a nuclear war in the small German town of Schewenborn. The tale is told through Peter's eyes, a young boy who, along with his family, faces the devastation and scarcity of a world transformed by nuclear fallout.  The story begins with the bombs falling, destroying everything Peter has ever known. The once idyllic town is now a nightmarish wasteland where food and water are scarce, and the threat of radiation sickness looms; Peter's family, once comfortably middle class, is reduced to scavenging for survival.  As the story progresses, Peter's parents and siblings succumb to radiation sickness, leaving him and his younger sister, Lisa, as the last children of Schewenborn. Despite the bleak circumstances, Peter and Lisa display remarkable resilience and courage, clinging to each other for emotional support and working together to find food and shelter.  The novel is a stark exploration of the human capacity for survival in the face of unimaginable adversity. It also serves as a powerful warning about the devastating consequences of nuclear warfare. Despite the grim subject matter, the story is ultimately about hope, resilience, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

Flemish Beef Roast (Or Stew) with Vegetables Recipe  Ingredients 1 2-3 pound beef roast, trimmed 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 1 large onion, chopped 2 carrots, chopped - 2 celery stalks chopped 3 cloves garlic, minced 1 teaspoon dried thyme 1 teaspoon dried rosemary 2 tablespoons tomato paste 1 cup beef broth 1 cup red wine 2 cups chopped mushrooms Salt and pepper to taste  Instructions 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. 2. Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium high heat. Add beef roast and brown on all sides about 8 minutes per side. Remove and set aside. 3. Add chopped onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme and rosemary to pot. Cook for about 5 minutes stirring occasionally until vegetables are softened. 4. Stir in tomato paste, beef broth, red wine and mushrooms. Bring to a simmer. 5. Season beef roast with salt and pepper. Place roast back in pot, spooning vegetable mixture on top. 6. Cover pot with a lid and transfer to preheated oven. Roast for about 1 hour and 15 minutes or until beef is tender and vegetables are cooked through. 7. Remove roast from pot and let rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving. Serve with vegetable mixture on the side. Enjoy.

Blue Merle was an American rock band from Los Angeles, California, United States. The band consisted of brothers Liam Finn (vocals, guitar) and Caleb Johnson (bass, keyboards) and sister Morgan Finn (drums, percussion). The band released two albums, Burning in the Sun (2003) and Keeps Me Wondering (2006) before breaking up in 2007.  Liam and Caleb Finn formed Blue Merle in 2002 after the dissolution of their previous band the Johnson Brothers. The pair were soon joined by their sister Morgan and the three began writing and performing together.  The band released their debut album, Burning in the Sun in 2003. The album was produced by T-Bone Burnett and featured the single "Halo".  The band's second album, Keeps Me Wondering, was released in 2006; The album was produced by Brendan O'Brien and featured the singles "Out of My Hands" and "Boxcar Racer".  The band toured extensively in support of both albums, performing with artists such as Bob Dylan, Sheryl Crow and John Mayer.  In 2007, the band announced that they were breaking up; Liam and Caleb Finn went on to form the band N. In a 2014 interview with The Huffington Post, Liam Finn stated that Blue Merle had "run its course" and that the band was "never really meant to be a long-term thing".

Tom Hanks has been announced as the lead actor in a biopic about Leonardo da Vinci, a famed artist and inventor from history. The movie will explore his life and work from his early years in Italy to his later achievements in France.  Hanks is no stranger to playing real-life figures on screen, having won critical acclaim for his portrayals in "Captain Phillips" (2013) and "A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood" (2019). He also received Oscar nominations for both roles.  The yet untitled project will be directed by David Koepp, who has directed "Jurassic Park" (1998) and "Lincoln" (2012) for which he received another Oscar nomination. Filming is expected to begin next year, with a release date set for 2023.  This isn't the first time that Hollywood has attempted to bring da Vinci's story to the big screen. In 2003, Mel Gibson starred in "The Agony and the Ecstasy" while in 1972, Charlton Heston played the artist in "Leonard, A Life of Leonard Bernstein (I)." However, it remains to be seen how this latest adaptation will differentiate itself from its predecessors.

Ingredients 1 cup unsalted butter, softened 1 cup all purpose flour 1 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 teaspoon salt 2 cups granulated sugar 1 cup (8 oz) jam (any flavor)  For the Dough 1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside. 3. In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar on medium high speed until light and fluffy, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. 4. For the Filling 5. Divide the dough into two equal parts. Roll each portion out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/4 inch (6 mm). Cut into rounds with a 2-inch (5-cm) cookie cutter. Place half the rounds on the prepared baking sheet. 6. Top each round with 1 teaspoon of jam. Place another round on top of the jam, pressing the edges gently to seal. 7. Bake for 15 minutes or until the edges are lightly browned. Allow to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. The novel chronicles the adventures of a young boy named Dick Sand, who is thrust into leadership after the captain and first mate are killed in a mutiny. Despite his youth and inexperience, Dick proves to be a natural leader, using his quick thinking and resourcefulness to navigate the challenges of the high seas.  As he travels the globe. Dick encounters a diverse cast of characters. Including a group of dangerous pirates, a mysterious woman being held captive, and a brilliant scientist on the run from the law. He must contend with treacherous storms, treacherous crew members, and a treacherous sea monster.  Despite the obstacles in his path, Dick remains determined to complete his mission and prove himself as a capable captain. Through his adventures, he learns valuable lessons about leadership, loyalty, and the importance of never giving up, even in the face of overwhelming danger.  As the story unfolds, Dick's character evolves from a naive and impulsive young boy to a confident and capable young man ready to face whatever challenges the sea may throw his way. The novel ends with Dick returning home, hailed as a hero for his bravery and ingenuity, and ready to embark on the next chapter of his life as a seasoned captain.

Leonti Mroveli born on January 29, 1978, in Tbilisi, Georgia is a poet and musician of Georgian-Armenian descent. He grew up in Batumi, Georgia on the Black Sea coast. In an interview with Bidzina Kheiladze, Mroveli revealed that his maternal grandfather Shalva Mroveli had migrated from Armenia during the Soviet era. His paternal grandparents were forced from Nakhchivan due to Soviet atrocities against their family.  Mroveli began composing his own songs from a young age, often incorporating his refugee experiences into his music. He drew inspiration from a variety of musical styles including pop rock, jazz, funk and blues. Unlike other Georgian musicians who have adopted Western music genres for commercial success, Mroveli prefers to maintain his authenticity in sound and lyrics. His songs often have catchy melodies and meaningful lyrics that address societal issues in Georgia, such as poverty, inequality and political unrest.  Mroveli performs in Georgia and has also made appearances abroad.

Sir George Martin, the orchestrator of hundreds of the Beatles' recordings, passed away at the age of 90. The news has sparked a wave of emotion and retrospectives on his life and work. Sir George was a brilliant producer and a gentleman who revolutionized popular music with the artists he supported, notably The Beatles. While he earned fame and fortune it was his work with the Beatles that brought him lasting fame. He was an arranger and talent developer whose admiration and respect extended to many musicians he worked with. Despite being known as a "pop" producer his versatility is evident in his collaborations with diverse artists  -  Matt Monro, Cilla Black, Gerry and the Pacemakers, Cheap Trick and Jeff Beck.  In his autobiography Summer of Love, Sir George recounts his early years as a Decca Records clerk detailing the incredible luck and good fortune that his career turned on. He was talented, driven and hardworking. But he was also fortunate in being in the right place at the right time. Sir George was fortunate to work with the Beatles when their career took off. Despite initial skepticism, his punctuality, love for music and sense of humor won them trust and respect. He emerged as indispensable, striving to fulfill the group's vision and desire for experimentation in the recording studio. As their success soared, Martin managed ambitious projects while navigating the demands of the group's members and associates.  For more than five decades Sir George remained connected to his work with the Beatles seeking to protect and promote their artistic legacy. Given his importance to the history of popular music, it is fitting that Sir George Martin has received a variety of awards  -  knighthood and that he has left an indelible mark on the industry he helped pioneer.

Mentone is a small unincorporated community in Newton County, Texas, United States. It is situated at the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 1486 and 3294, about 15 miles north of the county seat Newton; Mentone was established in the late 1800s as a railroad stop on the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railway. The community was named after Mentone, a town in the Alpes Maritimes department in southeastern France.  Throughout its history, Mentone has been primarily an agricultural community, with cotton and grains being the main crops grown in the area. In the early 20th century, Mentone had a population of around 200 residents with several businesses including a general store, a cotton gin and a school. The community also had a post office which operated from 1896 until the late 1960s.  Today Mentone remains a small, close-knit community with a population of around 50 residents. The community is known for its annual Fourth of July celebration, which includes a parade, a barbecue and fireworks. Mentone is also home to the Mentone Cemetery, which is the final resting place for many of the community's early residents.  Despite its small size, Mentone has a rich history and a strong sense of community. Many residents are descendants of the original settlers, and the community continues to thrive as a close-knit rural community in Texas.

Delightful Lemon Cake Recipe  Ingredients  2 cups all purpose flour  1 ½ teaspoons baking powder, ¼ teaspoon salt -3 large eggs, room temperature  1 cup granulated sugar  2 tablespoons lemon zest, and ¾ cup fresh lemon juice  1 cup buttermilk, room temperature, ½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled  2 teaspoons vanilla extract  For the glaze  1 cup powdered sugar -2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice  Instructions, 1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour.  2. In a medium sized bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.  3. In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated.  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.  5. Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed.  6. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  7. Allow the cake to cool completely before making the glaze. To make the glaze. Whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy.

Tibor Grasser, born in 1969, is an Austrian composer and pianist. He studied piano at the Vienna Conservatory with Karl Leister and composition with Friedrich Cerha.  Grasser's music is characterized by its use of dissonance, rhythmic complexity, and a wide range of dynamics. He has written works for solo piano, chamber ensembles, orchestras, and opera. His music has been performed by ensembles  -  the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra, the Kölner Ensemble, and the Ensemble Modern.  In addition to his work as a composer, Grasser is an accomplished pianist and has performed with artists  -  Gidon Kremer and Yehudi Menuhin. He has recorded several albums of his own music, including "Piano Concerto No. 1" and "Symphony No. 1."  Grasser's music has been praised for its emotional intensity and its ability to evoke a wide range of emotions. He has won numerous awards for his compositions, including the Ernst von Siemens Music Prize and the Joseph Haydn Prize.  Today Grasser continues to write and perform music and is considered one of the most important composers of his generation.

Ingredients, 1 head of broccoli, cut into small florets and 3 cloves of garlic, minced and 1/2 cup of ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup of grated parmesan cheese and 1/4 cup of hot honey 8 slices of bread and 2 tablespoons of olive oil  Instructions 1. Preheat your oven to 400°F.  2. In a large bowl, mix together the broccoli florets, minced garlic, olive oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper.  3. Spread the broccoli mixture onto a baking sheet and roast in the oven for 20-25 minutes. Until the broccoli is tender and slightly browned.  4. While the broccoli is roasting. Prepare the ricotta mixture. In a small bowl, mix together the ricotta cheese, parmesan cheese and a pinch of salt and pepper.  5. Once the broccoli is done. Remove it from the oven and reduce the temperature to 375°F.  6. Toast the bread slices in the oven for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden.  7. Remove the bread from the oven and spread a thin layer of ricotta mixture onto each slice.  8. Top each slice of bread with a generous spoonful of roasted broccoli and a drizzle of hot honey.  9. Serve immediately and enjoy your delicious Broccoli and Garlic Ricotta Toasts with Hot Honey.

Avi Gabbay, born on August 16, 1968, is an Israeli politician who served as the leader of the Labor Party from 2016 to 2019. He previously held the position of Knesset member for the party and was the Minister of Transportation and the Minister of Environmental Protection.  Gabbay was born in Tel Aviv and studied law at Tel Aviv University. He joined the Labor Party during his youth and first entered the Knesset in 2003. Over the years, he rose through the ranks, becoming the party's secretary-general from 2012 to 2016 before being elected as its leader in 2016.  While serving as transportation minister, Gabbay oversaw the construction of Jerusalem's light rail system and expanded the metro in Tel Aviv. He also promoted electric and hybrid vehicles and initiated a program to boost bicycle use.  As environmental protection minister, Gabbay implemented policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote renewable energy. He also worked to protect Israel's natural resources,  -  its beaches and parks.  In the 2019 Israeli legislative election, the Labor Party under Gabbay's leadership failed to win any seats in the Knesset, and Gabbay resigned as party leader. He subsequently left politics and returned to his private law practice.

Barry Holmes triumphs in comeback victory  Barry Holmes secured a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. The world number 39 trailed 6-2 to Mark Selby in the final but won eight of the next nine frames to triumph 10-7.  It is the first ranking event success for the 41-year old from Birmingham who has now earned £200,000 in prize money this season.  "I'm over the moon it's been a great week," Holmes said. "I've been working hard on my game and it's nice to get some reward for it."  Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back.  He levelled at 6-6 with a break of 106 and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames to move within one of victory.  The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46; Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title.  "I'm gutted to lose but I've got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable," Selby said. "I had my chances in the match, but I couldn't take them. I'm sure I'll be back stronger for it."

Coconut Fudge Brownies Recipe  Ingredients 1 cup of granulated sugar, ½ cup of softened butter, ¼ cup of melted coconut oil and 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour ¾ cup of unsweetened cocoa powder 2 teaspoons baking powder ½ teaspoon salt 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips ½ cup of shredded coconut  Instructions which are 1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.  2. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the sugar, butter and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.  3. In another medium sized bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.  4. Fold in the chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.  5. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  6. Allow the brownies to cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy.

This paper introduces a novel uncertainty aware self ensembling (UA SE) model for 3D left atrium segmentation in semi supervised learning. The UA SE model leverages correlations between neighboring voxels and employs a self ensemble strategy to boost the representation power of semi-supervised learning. Utilizing a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module, the model models spatial correlations and outputs an uncertainty map. Additionally, a self ensembling module is proposed that considers both labels and uncertainties by taking into account local graph structure. The model is trained semi-supervisedly, using only a small portion of labeled data for training and leveraging the remaining unlabeled data to enhance its representation power. The proposed method is evaluated on the MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset; Experimental results show the UA SE model's effectiveness compared to state of the art semi-supervised learning methods. The code and dataset are available at https, //github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE.

This paper explores the transition of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, to a two-dimensional (2D) state. Utilizing a blend of experimental and theoretical methods, we analyze Bi2Se3's electronic structure and topological characteristics as its thickness diminishes from 3D to 2D. Our findings reveal that the 3D Dirac cone transforms into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, leading to the formation of novel topological phases. We observe topologically protected edge states on the surfaces of the 2D system which are resilient to disorder and defects. Additionally, we identify non-trivial band structure and Fermi arc behavior in the 2D states indicating the presence of non-trivial topology. This research offers new perspectives on the transition of 3D topological insulators to 2D systems and opens avenues for further investigation into low-dimensional topological phenomena.

The future of home phones seems uncertain as more people are choosing mobile phones over landlines, according to a recent survey by Ofcom. The study found that the number of UK landline calls fell by 10% in 2020, marking a significant shift in communication habits.  The report indicates that the decline in landline usage is mainly due to the growing popularity of mobile phones and digital communication platforms like WhatsApp, Skype and Zoom. These platforms offer a variety of communication options  -  voice and video calls, text messaging and file sharing, making them a more versatile alternative to traditional landlines.  Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the shift towards digital communication. With many people working from home and social distancing measures in place, digital platforms have become the primary means of communication for both personal and professional purposes.  Despite the decline, landlines are still used by a significant number of people, particularly the elderly and those living in rural areas with poor mobile coverage. For these individuals, landlines provide a reliable and accessible means of communication.  However, the trend towards mobile and digital communication is likely to continue, raising questions about the future of home phones. Some experts predict that landlines may eventually become obsolete. While others believe they will continue to exist in a more limited capacity.  The telecommunications industry is also responding to this change. Many companies now offer packages that include broadband and mobile services but not landline. This reflects the changing needs and preferences of consumers, who increasingly value flexibility and convenience.  In conclusion, while the future of home phones is uncertain, it is clear that the way we communicate is evolving. As technology continues to advance, it will be interesting to see how traditional communication methods like landlines adapt to the digital age.

The US government is seeking a new ruling against tobacco companies that could cost them up to $280bn (£155bn). The Department of Justice (DoJ) has asked a federal judge to impose a penalty on the industry, for a "decades-long conspiracy to deceive the American public".  The move comes after a 2020 ruling in which the tobacco industry was found guilty of violating federal racketeering laws. The DoJ now wants the companies to surrender profits made through their alleged misconduct. Which it claims spanned more than 50 years.  The case, which is one of the largest civil cases in US history, targets major tobacco companies including Philip Morris USA, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, Brown & Williamson and Lorillard Tobacco. The government alleges that these companies deliberately misled the public about the health risks associated with smoking and the addictive nature of nicotine.  The $280bn figure is based on the government's estimate of profits from cigarette sales to underage smokers and smokers who were allegedly deceived by the companies' marketing tactics. The DoJ argues that these profits were ill-gotten and should be forfeited.  The tobacco industry has strongly denied the allegations and is expected to fight the penalty. They argue that the government's case is based on a flawed interpretation of the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), the law under which the case is being pursued.  The industry also contends that the penalty is excessive and would lead to bankruptcy for many companies, resulting in job losses and harm to the economy. They further argue that they have already paid billions in settlements to individual states, and have significantly changed their marketing practices in response to previous litigation.  The case is expected to be heard in the coming months. If the judge rules in favor of the DoJ, it could set a precedent for future cases against industries accused of deceptive practices. However, any ruling is likely to be appealed, potentially leading to years of further litigation.
